objective: T-20260930-01: does the Harvey-Mazzoleni-Melone 60/40 rebalancing-pressure signal (Threshold averaged over 25 deltas 0.1%..2.5%, Calendar last-week signal, weight W = 0.6*(-Threshold/0.012) + 0.4*CalendarMod), simulated from SPY and IEF closes, still forecast next-day SPY returns in the part a next-open fill can capture (the open-to-close leg) in 2016-2026 and in the 2024-01-08..2026-09-29 window, and does an equity-leg-only book (SPY, QQQ, TQQQ/SQQQ) clear a net Sharpe of 0.8 after 10 bp per side? Bond-leg spreads (R1, R2, R7) are diagnostics only because the owner rejected cross-asset trading on 2026-09-28.
target_regime_and_horizon: Daily signal, one-session hold; regression windows by return date: full 2016-01-05..2026-09-29, stress 2016-05-02..2023-08-31, anchor 2024-01-08..2026-09-29 (all frozen before results). Ledger windows (only if the gate passes) use scripts/screen_lane.py WINDOWS unchanged. Regime claim: post-2016, crowded-trade era; validity window and invalidation signal are the anchor-window coefficient sign and t.
existing_solution_comparison: Published: NBER w33554 (Sharpe 1.11 futures spread 1997-09..2023-03, 0.90 excluding 2008-09..2009-03 and 2020-03, roughly 1 net of authors' cost estimate) and QuantReturns independent replication (futures 1.42 2007..2025-06, SPY/TLT ETF version Sharpe 1.17, Beta 0.12, no costs, both legs traded). Not enough for us: both are close-to-close futures spreads with a bond leg (owner rejected cross-asset 2026-09-28), untradable at Alpaca as futures, and neither reports the overnight/intraday split or costs at a next-open fill. Local work fills exactly that gap: the equity leg only, ETF closes, open-to-close return, 10 bp per side.
remaining_evidence_gap: Where the 17 bp lives (overnight, invisible to a next-open fill, versus intraday) is unreported in the sources; whether the effect survives 2016-2026 after publication and crowding (Daniel: competition erodes liquidity-provision anomalies; Parker-Schoar-Sun: flows spread over months); the source Calendar rule differs between the paper (reversal on first business day, 1.5 percent normalisation) and QuantReturns (last session, 0.012) and the task fixes the QuantReturns version; SPY/IEF closes are not dividend-adjusted (verified against local adjusted data in the report).
negative_experiments_checked: oc research directions check rebalanc on 2026-09-30: no prior direction matching except the queued registry entry dir:pension_rebalancing_front_run_equity_leg. dir:index_rebalance_flow_prediction (not_executable 2026-09-28) is REOPENED: it said the paper has no strategy Sharpe and needs an index rebalancing calendar; the January 2026 revision Section 4 gives the rule and Sharpe, and the signal needs only SPY and IEF returns, no calendar. grep -ril rebalanc over iterations finds only h20260928_16_8k_sentiment_accel, h20260928_02_cross_asset_sleeve (static or unrelated) and older LETF rebalancing and S3 tranching work, none testing this mechanism. reports/research/signal-cards overnight_mom_21 and intraday_rev_21 found no signal on generic overnight/intraday effects, which does not test this signal.
cost_and_execution_assumptions: Frozen contract: signal at the close of t, fill at the open of t+1, 10 bp per side per leg on weight change (20 bp check), hold to close t+1 (open-to-close, primary, entry and exit each pay) or to open t+2 (open-to-open, reported); SPY/QQQ short borrow 0.3 percent per year (3 percent sensitivity) charged per session held short; TQQQ/SQQQ are long-only instruments; W>0 means long equity, W<0 short SPY/QQQ or long SQQQ. Sharpe via the frozen base.metrics with BIL as the risk-free leg.
stop_condition: Stage 1 gate (frozen, thresholds unchanged after seeing results): equity-leg (SPY) open-to-close Threshold regression coefficient negative, full-sample HC3 t <= -2.5, anchor-window same sign with |t| >= 2.0. If the effect sits in the overnight leg instead, write that it is not obtainable at a next-open fill and stop. If Stage 1 fails, no candidate ledger is run. If Stage 1 passes, continue only when at least one equity-leg candidate among R3, R4, R5, R6, R8 has 10 bp net Sharpe >= 0.8 full-sample and >= 0.8 anchor; then K1/K2 tiers, DSR over 8, 20 bp, random-date placebo <= 10 percent. Bond-leg candidates never advance without an owner decision.

sources.claim: Harvey, Mazzoleni and Melone (NBER w33554, March 2025, revised January 2026, full text read): a one-standard-deviation increase in the Threshold (Calendar) signal lowers next-day S&P 500 futures returns by about 16 (17) bp and raises 10-year Treasury futures returns by 4 (2) bp; the pressure reverts within two weeks; Section 4 front-running spread portfolio (long S&P 500 futures / short 10y note futures, weight = average of modified Threshold and Calendar signals) has Sharpe above 1 over 1997-2023.
sources.market_and_period: US S&P 500 and 10-year note futures, 1997-2023, close-to-close daily.
sources.applicability: Source of the Threshold and Calendar signal definitions, the next-day sign expectation (equity down when equity is overweight) and the two-week reversion horizon used to set the placebo shift range.
sources.limitations: Futures returns, close-to-close, not open-to-close; author-reported Sharpe with the authors' own cost estimate; multiple-comparison bias on signal windows flagged by the discussant; effect concentrated before the 2016 start of the local sample is not excluded.
sources.independent_replication: QuantReturns replication (2025) reproduces the sign and roughly the size; no independent live record found.

sources.claim: NBER abstract page (revision date January 2026): institutional rebalancing has a market-wide impact; equity returns fall 17 bp over the next day when stocks are overweight; cost to investors about 16 billion USD a year.
sources.applicability: Headline effect size the negation regression is measured against (the effect is a close-to-close 17 bp, larger than a 10 bp per side cost).
sources.limitations: Abstract only; close-to-close, not the overnight/intraday split that determines what a next-open fill can capture.

sources.claim: Paper Section 4 defines the modified Calendar signal as sign(-Calendar) in the last week (5 days) of a month, a reversal term sign(Calendar_{-4}) on the first business day of the new month, and zero on any other day; the Threshold part is rescaled to -Threshold/1.5% so both signals have equal risk contribution.
sources.applicability: Fixes the Calendar structure (last-week days plus one reversal day). The queue task and the QuantReturns replication use normalisation 0.012 and put the reversal on the last session of the month; the preregistration follows the task.
sources.limitations: Paper normalises by 1.5%, QuantReturns by 0.012, and the paper places the reversal on the first business day; the preregistered candidate uses the task's version and the difference is a disclosed deviation.

sources.claim: Parker, Schoar and Sun (NBER w28028, JF 2023): target date funds rebalance contrarianly between stocks and bonds within a few months; the flows reach stocks held through mutual funds and reduce their next-quarter returns.
sources.applicability: Independent evidence that the rebalancing flow exists and is spread over months, so a next-day-only signal captures only part of it.
sources.limitations: Quarterly horizon, cross-sectional stock effect; not a daily index timing rule; no Sharpe.
sources.independent_replication: Cited by Harvey et al. as supporting evidence.

sources.claim: Kent Daniel discussion slides (Red Rock 2025): the signal windows (thresholds 0.1-2.5 percent, calendar 5 days before month end) were selected among many, so the reported t-statistics are biased upward.
sources.applicability: Motivates the frozen out-of-window test (2016-2026 is after most of the source sample) and DSR over 8 trials.

sources.claim: Daniel: liquidity-provision anomalies (index inclusion, short-term reversal, leveraged ETF rebalancing) historically faded as competition rose, and the paper's 16 billion annual cost is a worst-case estimate.
sources.applicability: Prior that the effect decayed after publication (2025) and after the 2016 start of the local sample.
sources.limitations: Historical analogy, not a test on this signal.

sources.claim: QuantReturns replication (GitHub mirror of the 2025-07-03 article): Threshold signal averaged over deltas, divided by 0.012 and inverted; Calendar signal zero except the last five sessions of a month, minus sign for the first four, inverse of the 5th-last value on the last day; weight 0.6 Threshold + 0.4 Calendar; futures Sharpe 1.24 (1997-2025), 1.42 (2007-2025-06); SPY/TLT ETF version CAGR 15.62 percent, Sharpe 1.17, no costs.
sources.applicability: Concrete implementable formula for the modified Calendar signal.
sources.limitations: Author self-computed, not peer reviewed, no transaction costs, both legs traded, close-to-close.
sources.independent_replication: Reproduces the paper's shape; no third-party check.

sources.claim: Bloomberg (2025-02-05): front-running of scheduled pension and balanced-fund rebalancing by fast-money speculators is described as an open secret.
sources.applicability: Evidence that the trade is crowded, which is the decay risk to test in the 2024-2026 window.

cheapest_decisive_test.action: scripts/run_h20260930_01_rebalancing.py regress under scripts/run_capped.sh --mem 600M: SPY and SPY-IEF next-day return (overnight, intraday, total) on the Threshold signal (and Calendar variants), HC3, three windows, 500 date-shift placebos; reads only SPY, IEF, TLT, QQQ, TQQQ, SQQQ, BIL daily bars.
cheapest_decisive_test.pass_condition: SPY open-to-close Threshold coefficient negative, full-sample HC3 t <= -2.5 and anchor-window t <= -2.0.
cheapest_decisive_test.falsification_condition: Coefficient positive or |t| below either bar, or the effect concentrated in the overnight leg with intraday insignificant.
